key_insight: The paper shows that, under checkable conditions, a convergence certificate for a contact Hamiltonian ODE can be transferred to an order-r discrete contact splitting method with only controlled backward-error and step-size perturbations.
engineering_relevance: This gives optimization algorithm designers a principled way to turn continuous-time rate guarantees into discrete solver guarantees for structured methods such as heavy-ball, damped splittings, and other contact-based optimizers.
method: Define an augmented contact energy certificate using the Hamiltonian and its conformal decay rate.
Use backward error analysis to analyze the discrete splitting via a modified contact Hamiltonian.
Prove rate transfer through three named hypotheses and illustrate it on quadratic heavy ball and strongly convex, state-dependent damping cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments that match the predicted conformal-factor tracking orders and show competitive performance on ill-conditioned benchmarks and deep-learning tasks.
watch_item: The guarantee depends on verifying the three transfer hypotheses and on staying within the finite backward-error horizon, so the certificate may weaken for larger steps or poorly matched splittings.
paper_title: When Rates Are Geometric: Rate-Certificate Transfer for Contact Splittings in Optimization
